Hi, Dr. [Your Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I... well, I guess I'm just here because I've been feeling a little off lately. It's probably nothing major, I mean, everyone gets stressed, right? I'm a teacher, so it's a busy job. But... I've just been having these thoughts, and I wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in. Is it okay to talk about that? 

I just... sometimes, lately, I catch myself thinking that it might just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And, um, on the drive home from school, I sometimes wonder if my family and my students might actually be better off without me. Which sounds terrible, I know, and I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything. It actually scares me to think that way, because I really don't want to do anything to hurt myself. I'm just... I'm hoping maybe you can tell me if that's normal to feel sometimes?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, even activities or hobbies that you typically find rewarding or pleasurable?

Um, well, I guess maybe a little bit? I try really hard to keep up with everything, I promise I do. Usually, I really look forward to things like playing softball, or going to my book club. And I love my garden, and I help run the robotics club at school... but lately, I don't know, I guess I've just been kind of going through the motions with all of it. 

Sometimes I even end up canceling, which I feel absolutely awful about because I hate letting people down. It's just that none of it really feels enjoyable right now. I'm probably just letting work stress get to me, right? I really hope I don't sound lazy for saying that... is it normal to lose interest in things like that when you're overwhelmed?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels lately, like feeling more tired than usual even after resting or finding it hard to get through your day?

Um, well... I mean, teaching is naturally pretty exhausting, right? I'm sure most people are tired after work. But... I guess I have been feeling a bit more drained than usual. I really try to push through it, I promise, because I don't want to let my performance slip or be a burden on anyone. 

It's just... lately, by the time I get through teaching for the day, and then maybe a department meeting, my body just feels so heavy. It sounds silly, and I really shouldn't complain, but even doing little things at home, like making dinner or just trying to answer a few parent emails... it honestly feels like climbing a huge hill. I hope I don't sound like I'm just making excuses or being weak. Do you think that's just normal burnout from the school year?
Have you had any trouble sleeping lately, like waking up in the middle of the night or waking up earlier than you planned and not being able to fall back asleep?

Um, well... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. But honestly, it's probably just my own fault for worrying too much. I mean, I'll be completely exhausted when I get into bed, but then I just lie awake... I end up replaying all my upcoming assessment deadlines, or agonizing over little classroom mistakes I made that day. 

I really try to just shut my brain off, I promise, because I know I need to be rested and sharp for my students. But then, even when I do finally fall asleep, I usually end up waking up around 4 a.m., and... I never really get back to sleep after that. I just sort of lie there. I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm terrible at managing my stress... is it pretty common for people to have sleep issues like that when they have a lot on their plate?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the time lately, even when there’s no specific reason for it?

Um, well... I wouldn't really say I've been feeling depressed, exactly. I mean, I have so much to be grateful for, you know? A good job, great students... I really shouldn't be complaining at all. 

I guess I've just been feeling a little bit off lately, maybe? Like, just kind of flat or stressed. But I really try to keep a positive attitude, I promise. I always put on a smile for my classes because they deserve my best energy. I'm sure it's just normal stress, right? I mean, everyone has days where they feel a little less than perfect, don't they? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Can you recall if there have been days when you truly didn’t care about doing things you usually enjoy, like your book club or gardening, and it felt like nothing could bring you pleasure?

Um, well... I mean, I definitely still think those things are important. I really love my book club, and the robotics club at school is such a great group of kids. I don't want you to think I've just given up on them or anything. 

I guess... I have been maybe missing a few more things than usual lately. Like, I used to really look forward to my softball league and spending time in my garden on the weekends. But recently, I've just been... well, I've canceled a few times. Or if I do go to book club or robotics, I'm sort of just going through the motions, you know? It's probably just because I'm so focused on my lesson plans and I don't want to spread myself too thin. But honestly, it just hasn't felt as fun or enjoyable as it used to. I feel terrible even saying that, because I know people count on me to be there and be engaged. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound selfish or lazy.
Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you're not good at things you used to feel confident about, even at work or in your personal life?

Um, well... I definitely don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or anything. I know I'm very capable, and I try my hardest every day. But... I guess I have been struggling a little bit with my confidence lately. 

It's just... if a lesson doesn't go exactly right, or if I see a student looking confused, I immediately feel like I'm just letting everyone down. I know I shouldn't, but I end up replaying it in my head over and over, and I start thinking that I'm just a terrible teacher... and honestly, a terrible mother, too, because I bring that stress home. I really try to shake it off, I promise. I know it's probably just my own insecurities acting up, and I should be stronger than that. Is it normal to be so hard on yourself when you're feeling stressed out? I just don't want you to think I'm totally incompetent.
Can you tell me if there have been days when you truly didn’t care about doing things you usually enjoy, like your book club or gardening, and it felt like nothing could bring you pleasure?

Oh, um... yeah, I know I touched on this a little bit just a few minutes ago, but... I guess if I'm being completely honest about it... yes. 

I really hate admitting it, because I don't want to sound like a flake to my friends or the students. But I used to genuinely look forward to all of it—my softball games, the book club, working out in my garden, and the robotics club. Now... I don't know, I just end up canceling a lot of the time. And when I do push myself to show up, I'm mostly just going through the motions. It's like... none of it really feels enjoyable anymore, no matter how hard I try to put on a brave face and participate. 

I feel so guilty even saying that out loud, because I know how lucky I am to have these groups. Do you think that's just a normal part of being overwhelmed? I really hope I'm not just being lazy.

Um, I know we just talked about this, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much... I don't want to waste your time. But, um, yes, I suppose that's true. 

I mean, I love my family, of course, and I always want to be there for them. But with the other things... my garden, the softball league, my book club, and the robotics kids... I used to just love all of that so much. It was the highlight of my week. But lately, I just... I find myself canceling on them. Or if I do manage to get myself there, I'm really just going through the motions. It's like the joy is just kind of... gone right now. 

I feel awful admitting that, because it sounds so ungrateful, doesn't it? I know I should be appreciating these things more. I'm really trying to get back to my old self, I promise. I just hope you don't think I'm a bad person for feeling this way.
Have you noticed that even the things you used to really enjoy, like your garden or time with family, don’t bring you any pleasure at all lately?

Oh, gosh... I feel terrible, I must not be explaining myself very well since we keep coming back to this. I'm so sorry if I'm being confusing or not giving you the right details!
